robot.name: Figure 02
robot.status_notes: Figure describes Figure 02 as retired after Figure 03; BMW later published Figure 02 production metrics for 2025.

runtime.notes: Reported by hellonoid.com, added 2026-10-29 by automated spec fill; Battery life/autonomous runtime listed by a third-party aggregator; not confirmed on Figure's own page..

battery.notes: Launch release says Figure 02 has a custom 2.25 kWh battery pack and more than 50 percent more energy than Figure 01.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Public sources reviewed did not provide total robot degrees of freedom.

walking_speed.notes: Reported by hellonoid.com, added 2026-10-29 by automated spec fill; Walking speed..

hands.description: Fourth-generation human-scale hands; Figure says each hand has 16 active degrees of freedom and human-equivalent strength.

compute.description: Launch release claims three times more onboard computation and AI inference than Figure 01.

actuators.description: Launch release describes a redesigned exoskeleton and integrated wiring.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: BMW-confirmed production work involved removing and positioning sheet-metal components for welding; Figure demos show broader grasping and logistics manipulation.
caveats: BMW task is narrow industrial handling.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: BMW reported 10-hour shifts and large part counts in 2025 production; intervention rate and autonomy boundaries were not disclosed.
caveats: Strong task-output evidence, but not a full autonomy disclosure.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Official demos show biped walking and learned walking behavior; BMW evidence implies workcell operation.
caveats: No independent mobility benchmark, walking speed, or fall-rate metric found.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Figure describes six RGB cameras and Helix vision-language-action demos involving object recognition and manipulation.
caveats: Scene understanding is company-demo evidence, not independent benchmarking.

human_interaction.summary: Launch materials state Figure 02 includes microphones and speakers for speech interaction through AI models trained with OpenAI.
caveats: No independent conversational reliability test found.

endurance_reliability.summary: BMW reported Figure 02 supported 10-hour weekday shifts, more than 90,000 components, about 1.2 million steps, and about 1,250 operating hours.
caveats: Public metric is from one customer context and task family.

human_environment_fit.summary: The robot is human-sized and operated in a BMW automotive plant workcell designed around human-scale production tasks.
caveats: Evidence is industrial, not home or public-space operation.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: BMW signed a commercial agreement and later reported measurable Figure 02 production support at Spartanburg.
caveats: Only BMW has customer-confirmed public metrics in the reviewed sources.
No public price or purchase path found.

evidence_items.title: Figure 02 launch specifications
evidence_items.claim: Figure launched Figure 02 with six RGB cameras, a 2.25 kWh battery, three times more onboard compute than Figure 01, and 16 active DoF per hand.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Launch release listed cameras, battery capacity, compute increase, and hand DoF.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official company launch source; not independent verification.

evidence_items.title: BMW commercial agreement
evidence_items.claim: Figure announced a commercial agreement with BMW Manufacturing to bring general-purpose robots into automotive production.
evidence_items.notes: Company announcement; later BMW sources are stronger.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Figure announced a BMW commercial agreement for automotive production.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Agreement context only; measured deployment comes from later BMW source.

evidence_items.title: BMW Spartanburg production metrics
evidence_items.claim: BMW said Figure 02 supported more than 30,000 BMW X3 vehicles, handled more than 90,000 components, made about 1.2 million steps, and accumulated about 1,250 operating hours.
evidence_items.notes: Strongest public evidence found because it is customer-confirmed and measured.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Direct evidence for useful task execution and reliability.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: BMW reported operating hours, components handled, steps, shifts, and vehicle-production support.
evidence_items.source_location: BMW Group deployment article production-metrics section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Strongest customer-confirmed evidence in the pack.

evidence_items.title: Figure BMW retrospective
evidence_items.claim: Figure reported an 11-month BMW deployment, active assembly-line launch within 10 months, and Figure 02 retirement after Figure 03 release.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Helps establish lifecycle and deployment cadence.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Figure described BMW deployment cadence and Figure 02 retirement after Figure 03.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company deployment retrospective; use BMW for customer metrics.

evidence_items.title: Helix manipulation demos
evidence_items.claim: Figure's Helix materials show Figure 02 robots manipulating varied household and logistics objects with a vision-language-action model.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Relevant to broader manipulation, below customer deployment proof.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Helix demo pages show object handling and logistics-style manipulation.
evidence_items.source_location: Figure Helix and Helix Logistics demo pages
evidence_items.verification_notes: Observable company demos separated from claims about general autonomy.

evidence_items.title: RL walking demo
evidence_items.claim: Figure published a reinforcement-learning walking update showing learned biped locomotion on Figure 02.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Figure walking update shows learned biped walking behavior.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company mobility demo; no independent measurements.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: Figure 02 has unusually strong customer-confirmed deployment evidence through BMW, but broad generality still rests mostly on company demos.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No public price or purchase path.
No disclosed intervention or failure rate.
No total DoF, walking speed, or runtime metric found.
do_not_overclaim: Do not describe Figure 02 as currently purchasable.
Do not treat Helix demos as independent proof of open-ended autonomy.
Do not generalize BMW's specific task to all human work.

currentness.currentness_notes: Figure 02 has customer-confirmed historical deployment evidence but is treated as superseded by Figure 03.

excluded_claims.reason: No public Figure 02 price or purchase path was found, and Figure describes the model as retired/superseded.

excluded_claims.claim: Independent benchmark-level manipulation or locomotion scores
excluded_claims.reason: Reviewed sources include customer deployment and company demos, but no independent benchmark.
Strongest evidence is a narrow BMW industrial workflow; home/logistics breadth is company-demo evidence.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Figure 02 is a superseded second-generation Figure humanoid with strong customer-confirmed BMW production evidence, including operating hours and output metrics. Its broader manipulation/autonomy claims should be interpreted conservatively because they mostly come from company demos.
strongest_evidence: Official specs for hands, cameras, battery, and compute.
